findings.title: Forcing Deployment on exclusive leaves breaks valid Java DESCRIPTION inputs that still require interface parsing
findings.evidence: Both fresh_file_interface_component_mix and fresh_agent_interface_component_mix are valid under the Java oracle. In each case Java renders an interface entity between the component and the exclusive leaf, but Rust's no-oracle product output never emits that Java interface node once the exclusive leaf forces UmlSubtype::Deployment.
findings.interpretation: The mechanism claim is false at the Component/Deployment capability boundary. An exclusive leaf does reject the Rust Component candidate, but the chosen Rust Deployment path cannot consume the full valid Java DESCRIPTION surface that remains in the same source.

findings.title: The shared artifact/storage control still diverges, but not for the rejecting reason
findings.evidence: fresh_artifact_storage_interface_controls keeps artifact and storage on the shared side, yet Rust renders the artifact with default rx/ry 2.5 instead of Java's generic-roundcorner rx/ry 8.5.
findings.interpretation: This prevents a clean positive control story, but it is best attributed to adjacent round-corner behavior rather than to the dispatch rule that this review is checking.

verdict_reason: Fresh valid held-outs disprove the implemented dispatch rule. Rust now forces Deployment when file or agent appears, but the resulting Deployment parser cannot preserve shared Java DESCRIPTION interface syntax that remains valid in the same source. Under the T14 held-out rule, those counterexamples reject the change.
